folder.description: The folder on the machine the connector was set up on.

repo.description: The folder's git origin, which finds or clones it on a machine without that folder.

args.description: `claude` arguments, with `EXE_PLACEHOLDER` where the pinned binary goes.

token.description: The account's GitHub token, added by the hub, which clones a private repository.

account.description: The agent account the connector names; none runs the session under its project's.

Provider.description:
One row per agent CLI pinned can host. A table, so adding a provider is one entry, not a
branch per call site.

oneOf.description: Marks a draft ready for review.
Turns an open pull request back into a draft.
Opens a pull request that undoes this merged one.
Merges once the required checks and reviews pass, by the method named.
Deletes a merged pull request's branch on GitHub.
The working tree, untracked files too, against HEAD.
The working tree against where HEAD left the default branch.

Filters.description: T3 Code's list filters, each one of GitHub's search qualifiers.

labels.description: A row holds a label of every group; a group's names are GitHub's own OR.

Price.description: A price the user set for a model, in USD per million tokens; cache prices left out are input's.

GitStep.description: One step of the header's Git action, which the page runs in order to show where it is.

oneOf.description: A commit message for `files`, or every change, written by a headless claude.
Commits `files`, or every change, with `message`.
Pushes the branch, setting its upstream on `origin` the first time.
Opens a pull request of the branch with gh, titled and described from its commits.
Fast-forwards the branch to its upstream.
Makes the folder a git repository.
Creates `name` on GitHub with gh, as `origin`, and pushes to it.

runOnWorktreeCreate.description: Runs in a new worktree as it is made for a thread.

async.description: With `run_on_worktree_create`, claude starts only once the script exits.

runOnSettle.description: Runs in a thread's worktree when the thread settles.

side.description: `RIGHT` for the new side, `LEFT` for a removed line.

PrChange.description: A change to who is on a pull request, what is on it, and its review threads.

oneOf.description: Adds or takes back the viewer's `content` on `subject`, a comment, review or the pull request.
Asks `login`, a person or a team's `org/slug`, for a review, or takes the request back.
Resolves the review thread `thread`, or opens it again.
Rewrites the comment `id`, a remark on the pull request or, with `review`, on a line.

Reaction.description: GitHub's reactions, by the name its GraphQL API gives them.

oneOf.description: Merges the pull request and the unmerged layers under it, as GitHub's merge-async does.
Rebases every unmerged layer, bottom to top, onto the stack's base.

StackHead.description: A layer's head as the reader last saw it, so a stack that moved since is not acted on.

HubCall.description:
Account-level calls, answered by the hub. Names and arguments match the app's Tauri
commands, so the settings page sends either. The last three come only from machines,
forwarding a connector session's callbacks to the hub, which holds the keys.

`{"cmd":"connect_linear","key":"lin_api_…"}`, `{"cmd":"stage","connector":"c1","issue":"uuid","stage":"coding"}`

`linear::Account`.
`connectors::Suggestions`.
`slack::Account`.
Channel names.
`github::Account`.
`Vec<github::Repo>`, most recently pushed first.

The folder of `repo` on `machine`, cloned there with the account's GitHub token when it has
none, or into `dest` when given.
`Vec<sync::Project>`: the account's projects, most recently shared first.
From a machine: a project it syncs, which other machines then offer to clone.
From a machine: `Vec<sync::Entry>`, every file the hub holds for the project.
From a machine: `null`, once the hub keeps the files.
From a machine: `Vec<sync::File>`.
The connector as stored.
`Vec<MachineView>`.
`PairCode`.
A signed-out app's connectors, moved to the account on its first sign-in.

What a connector's session works on, which its callbacks into pinned report against.
Untagged, so a stage message from a Linear session reads `"issue": "<id>"` as it always has.

anyOf.title: LinearIssue
anyOf.description: Linear's id for the issue, which `pinned stage` moves.

anyOf.title: SlackThread
anyOf.description: The Slack thread `pinned slack reply` answers in, and whose filed issue `pinned stage` moves.

Project.description: A project of the account, offered on machines that don't have it yet.

repo.description: The origin as the machine that shared it has it, which clones it elsewhere.

File.description: A file as the hub holds it. An empty `sha` marks a deleted one.

modified.description: Unix milliseconds the file last changed on the machine that sent it.

data.description: The contents gzipped, in base64; none for a deleted file.

model.description: Passed to `claude --model`; empty keeps claude's default.

worktree.description: Runs each session in its own git worktree, so parallel issues don't share a checkout.

since.description:
Only issues created after this instant (RFC 3339) trigger, so saving a connector
doesn't start sessions for the backlog. Slack connectors move it forward on every check.

handled.description: Issues, or Slack threads as `<channel id>:<thread ts>`, that already started a session.

team.description: The Linear team a Slack connector's sessions file issues in, by name or key.

label.description: The Linear label put on the issues a Slack connector's sessions file; empty puts none.

fix.description: Whether a Slack connector's sessions may file a Linear issue and fix the bug.

created.description: The issue each Slack thread's session filed, by `<channel id>:<thread ts>`.

followed.description: How far each handled Slack thread was passed on to its session, by `<channel id>:<thread ts>`.

proof.description: Whether a session that opens a pull request must prove it works, with a Playwright video.

account.description: The account its sessions run under; empty runs them under their project's.

oneOf.description: A Linear issue created with this label.
A Slack message in this channel, by name or id, that mentions the bot.

Columns.description: The Linear column each stage moves the issue to. Empty leaves the issue where it is.

Fix.description: How far a Slack connector's session goes with a bug it finds.

oneOf.description: Analyze and reply; never file an issue or change code.
Analyze, then ask in the thread; file and fix only once someone answered it with a mention.
Fix obvious bugs right away, and ask about the rest.

Filed.description: A Linear issue a Slack thread's session filed.

cursor.description: The newest message the session has seen, as a Slack ts.

seen.description: The newest message pinned read, when people wrote past `cursor` without mentioning the bot.

replied.description: Someone mentioned the bot in the thread after its session started, which `Fix::Ask` waits for.

RunsOn.description:
Where a workflow's sessions run. Kept under the connector's original `machine` key: a machine
id string ("" = any), or `{"kind":"upstash-box",…}`. Old stores load as before, and an old UI
that never touches the select saves the object back untouched.

Stage.description: Where a connector's session is in its work on an issue. Each stage maps to a Linear column.

oneOf.description: The harness picked the issue up and opened a session for it.
The session is about to change code.
The session opened the pull request.
